policies.title: Nicaragua: named Category A ordinary passports visa-free
policies.summary: The current official CA-4 AIP schedule explicitly marks these ordinary passports Category A (exempt from visa). It is a visa-free baseline, not an ETA, eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: The AIP says Category A nationals need a valid passport and admission by the migration officer at the arrival port; individual admission remains controlled.
The Tourist Card is a separate paid personal tourist document. It is not an ETA, eVisa or visa on arrival and does not change the Category A visa classification.
No duration, extension, onward-travel, funds, accommodation, health, fee-exemption or special-document rule is inferred beyond the cited sources.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, territorial and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Nicaragua: named Category B ordinary passports require consular visa
policies.summary: The current official CA-4 AIP schedule expressly marks these ordinary passports Category B: consular/no-consultation. The baseline is visa_required because the schedule requires a consular visa stamped before arrival, not an eVisa or ETA.
conditions: The AIP states that Category B nationals must present a passport and carry a stamped consular visa before the migration officer admits them at the arrival port.

The migration digest says a Category B visa may be issued at a migration post only under ratified instruments and migration policies. It does not identify a nationality-wide border-issued route for this cohort, so no visa_on_arrival route is inferred.
No online application, duration, fee, entries, extension, onward-travel, funds, accommodation, health or admission outcome is inferred.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, territorial and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Nicaragua: Indian ordinary passports eligible for a border-issued visa
policies.summary: The current official CA-4 AIP schedule uniquely marks Indian ordinary passports Category B ‘consular or border-issued’. Nicaragua’s migration law likewise describes Category B as consular-without-consultation or border visa. The border-issued route is normalized as visa_on_arrival, not eVisa or ETA.
conditions: The same ordinary-passport row also permits a consular route; this policy records the expressly available border-issued route as the nationality baseline.
The Special Tourist Card is a separate paid personal tourist document, is not an arrival visa, and is not valid for nationals subject to visa restrictions.
No online application, duration, fee, entries, extension, onward-travel, funds, accommodation, health or admission outcome is inferred.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, territorial and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Nicaragua: named Category C ordinary passports require advance consulted visa
policies.summary: The current official CA-4 AIP schedule expressly marks these ordinary passports Category C (consulted visa). It is an advance-authorization and consular route, normalized as visa_required rather than eVisa, ETA or visa on arrival.
conditions: The AIP requires the traveller or sponsor to request a Directorate-General of Migration and Foreigners endorsement through the relevant consulate before entry.

The migration digest assigns consulted visas for restricted-country nationals to the Directorate General of Migration and Foreigners; consular offices transmit applications and notification follows its decision.
The cited law gives consulted visas a 30-day validity and allows extension up to 90 days, except five-day transit visas; the actual visitor purpose, grant and admission remain case-specific.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, territorial and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Nicaragua: CA-4 national ordinary-passport entry
policies.summary: The official Assembly record describes the CA-4 agreement as suppressing visas and permitting each national to move among Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras and Nicaragua. This establishes the ordinary-passport visa-free baseline for the other three CA-4 nationalities.
conditions: The source describes regional free movement; this candidate records only the ordinary-passport visa outcome, not identity-card or other document alternatives.
No tourist-card exception, duration, fee, extension, onward-travel, funds, accommodation, health or port rule is inferred for this nationality cohort.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Nicaragua: citizen entry
policies.summary: Nicaragua’s current migration digest expressly says that no Nicaraguan needs an entry visa to enter Nicaragua; this is recorded as citizenship rather than visitor visa-free access.
conditions: This is a citizenship/right-of-entry rule, not a visitor route and not an ETA, eVisa, visa on arrival, Tourist Card or advance visa.
The source also addresses national document and age-specific departure rules; those are outside this ordinary-passport entry classification.
